tools.name: GetSuperInvestors
tools.title: Superinvestor Directory
tools.description: Get the curated superinvestor directory — a hand-picked list of well-known value investors and fund managers (Buffett, Ackman, Burry, Klarman and more), each with their 13F filer CIK and latest reported portfolio value, position count, quarter-over-quarter change, and report date. Portfolio value covers long US-listed 13F positions only, not total firm AUM; as-of dates vary by filer, and rows lagging the group's latest quarter are marked (stale). Use the returned CIK with GetInstitutionPortfolio for a manager's full holdings, or GetInstitutionQuarterlyActivity for their latest buys and sells.

tools.name: GetSupplyChain
tools.title: Supply Chain
tools.description: Get a company's supply chain: the customers, suppliers, competitors and partners named in annual reports (10-K, 20-F, 40-F and annual reports filed outside the US in English, another European language or Simplified Chinese) and in the quarterly reports (10-Q, Canadian MD&A), press releases, 8-Ks, earnings calls and mainland Chinese exchange announcements between them, its own and those of other listed companies that name it, with any stated revenue or receivables share, a revenue share in dollars from the same filing, the verbatim sentence and the source filing. A share belongs to the filing that states it. Names the filings never state are not inferred, so a missing company is not evidence of no relationship. Requires the Pro plan.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, QRVO), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XBRU:BAR) for a listing outside the US.

maxResults.description: Maximum companies listed per side (customers, suppliers, competitors, partners) (default: 50, max: 500). A company and the parts listed under it are kept together.

side.description: Only one side: customers, suppliers, competitors or partners (default: all four).

quantifiedOnly.description: Only companies with a stated revenue or receivables share (default: false).

lens.description: Order within each side: 'stated' (largest stated share first, the default), 'dependsOn' (largest share of this company's revenue first: who it relies on) or 'dependents' (largest share of the other company's own revenue first: who relies on it). A share is stated by a filing or derived from a stated share in dollars.

tools.name: GetSupplyChainOverlap
tools.title: Supply Chain Overlap
tools.description: Get which of a company's suppliers and customers also supply or buy from its competitors, as annual and quarterly reports, press releases, 8-Ks, earnings calls and mainland Chinese exchange announcements name them: each one with the listed competitors it also serves, or, with vs, the company against one competitor (both, only the company, only the competitor). A competitor whose own annual report is not read yet is marked, since other filings alone can miss what it uses. Requires the Pro plan.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g., NVDA), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:SU) for a listing outside the US.

vs.description: One competitor to compare with, by the symbol GetSupplyChain lists for it (e.g., AMD); omit to check every listed competitor.

maxResults.description: Maximum companies listed per side and group (default: 50, max: 500).

tools.name: GetTopGovernmentContractors
tools.title: Top Federal Contractors
tools.description: Rank public companies by total federal contract dollars awarded over a date range, one country at a time: US (default, from USAspending.gov; total award value of prime contract awards of $1M or more) or CA (Government of Canada contracts over C$10,000, contract value including amendments, in Canadian dollars, for vendors whose name exactly matches a company listed on a Canadian exchange). Unlisted recipients are excluded. Answers questions like 'which public companies won the most federal contracts last quarter'. Use GetGovernmentContracts for one company's individual awards.

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format, filtering on the award action date (defaults to 1 year ago)

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of companies to return (default: 25, largest first)

tools.name: GetTopHolders
tools.title: Top Institutional Holders
tools.description: Get the top institutional holders (fund managers) of an exact stock or ETF listing from SEC 13F-HR filings. Returns a ranked list by shares held, including published position value and percentage of total institutional 13F shares (not of shares outstanding). Values normally use report-date closing prices, may fall back to filer values, and can be zero when unavailable. During the newest quarter's filing window, non-ETF primary stocks carry non-filers' prior-quarter positions, each marked as carried and valued at its own quarter's close; ETF listings remain exact and as-filed because carry-forward is filer-wide. Use position type before treating put/call rows as ownership. A prior holder whose book is withheld under SEC confidential treatment is named below the list, unranked. Each holder shows its entity type from regulatory records (Form ADV, SEC filer profile, 13D/13G, N-CEN), filtered by holderTypes, and its style band measured from its filed book, filtered by styles.

ticker.description: Listed security ticker (e.g., AAPL, VOO)

reportDate.description: Quarter-end 13F report date in YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. 2026-03-31 (defaults to the latest available, or for a delisted company its last quarter on or before the delisting; an off-quarter date snaps to the nearest report on or before it)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of holding rows to return (default: 20, clamped to 1-500)

offset.description: Number of ranked holding rows to skip before returning results (default: 0)

holderTypes.description: Holder types to keep, as an array of tokens: adv (registered investment adviser), era (exempt reporting adviser), ia (other adviser), bank, ins (insurer), bd (broker-dealer), fund (registered fund), plan (benefit plan), nonus (non-US institution), hc (parent holding company or control person with no other type on record), unk (no deciding record yet), e.g. ["bank", "ins"]. Types come from Form ADV, SEC filer profiles, 13D/13G and N-CEN, never from names. Omit for all.

styles.description: Style bands to keep, as an array of tokens: idx (index-like), sys (systematic-like), conc (concentrated), divact (diversified active), unk (book too small or unvalued to band), e.g. ["conc"]. Bands are measured from each holder's filed 13F book in the newest measured quarter on or before the report date; a holder not measured that quarter is left out by any style filter. Omit for all.

tools.name: GetTopInstitutionalBuyersSellers
tools.title: Top Institutional Buyers and Sellers
tools.description: Get the institutions that moved the needle the most on a stock this quarter — biggest absolute share additions (Top Buyers) and biggest absolute share reductions (Top Sellers) versus the previous 13F report date. Includes new positions (Δ = full position) and sold-out positions (Δ = −prior position); entries and exits require observed 13F filings in both compared quarters, so missing filings cannot become a full-position buy or sale; a filer that continues under one new CIK with a matching 13F book is compared through that successor, and one split across several new CIKs is left out; the output counts the filers and shares left out and names the largest. While the newest quarter's filing window is open, results cover only the funds that have already filed (noted in the output). Returns a markdown table with two sections. Use this to surface the most actionable quarterly signal from 13F filings. Share changes count common shares only; an option position is not a buy or a sale.

ticker.description: Listed security ticker (e.g., AAPL, VOO)

reportDate.description: Quarter-end 13F report date in YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. 2026-03-31 (defaults to the latest available, or for a delisted company its last quarter on or before the delisting; an off-quarter date snaps to the nearest report on or before it)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of buyers and sellers to return per section (default: 10, clamped to 1-500)

tools.name: GetTranscriptPhraseTrend
tools.title: Transcript Phrase Trend
tools.description: Count how often a word or phrase comes up on a company's last earnings calls, oldest first: mentions per call, the rate per 10,000 words, the split between prepared remarks and Q&A where the call states its hand-off to questions, and one or two short quotes. Whole-word and case-insensitive, so "AI" never matches "said"; spellings that differ by a hyphen or a join count together ("copilot" also finds "co-pilot"), and the calls list which spelling they used. A call with no transcript text, or one in Chinese, Japanese or Korean, is flagged, never zero. Use it to follow a product, risk or initiative across quarters.

ticker.description: Company ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:AIR) for a listing outside the US.

phrase.description: Word or phrase to count, 2-80 characters after trimming (e.g. "tariffs", "sovereign AI"). Matched as whole words, ignoring case. A space or hyphen between words matches any whitespace, a hyphen or no gap ("co-pilot" finds "co pilot" and "copilot"), and a hyphen may split a word between two letters ("copilot" finds "co-pilot"); numbers never join, so "2025" never counts "20-25".

calls.description: Number of most recent earnings calls to read (default 8, max 12; values outside 1-12 are clamped)

tools.name: GetUpcomingInvestorEvents
tools.title: Upcoming Investor Events
tools.description: Get upcoming investor-relations events for a stock — earnings webcasts, conference appearances, presentations, and shareholder meetings — scraped from the company's IR website. Returns events scheduled from now onward, soonest first, optionally filtered by event type. Also states the next earnings call when one is known beyond the listed events: a scheduled call, or an estimate projected from the company's past call dates and labelled as one. Coverage is partial — an empty answer distinguishes a coverage gap from a genuinely empty calendar. Only future events are returned; for past events and their transcripts use ListInvestorEvents / GetInvestorEventTranscript.

ticker.description: Company ticker symbol (e.g., NVDA, AAPL), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:AIR) for a listing outside the US.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of events to return (default: 20, max: 500)

eventType.description: Optional event-type filter: EarningsCall, Conference, Presentation, ShareholderMeeting, or Webcast. Omit for all types. Events whose source label could not be classified carry the generic type 'Event' and only appear when no filter is set.

tools.name: GetValuationMultiples
tools.title: Valuation Multiples
tools.description: Get current EV/Revenue, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA, trailing and forward P/E, Price/Sales and Price/Book with peer median, quartiles and sample size; REITs add company-stated P/FFO and P/AFFO, and a verified reconciliation adds EV over Adjusted EBITDA. TTM flows use four discrete quarters or an exact annual-plus-YTD bridge, never an annual alone. P/E uses validated diluted EPS or income available to common, basis named. EV/EBITDA adds TTM D&A to TTM operating income. Forward P/E uses consensus EPS, possibly adjusted, for the next fiscal year. EV uses same-date reported debt, cash and short-term investments. Inputs reconcile, share one split basis and are USD; nothing is estimated. Peers exclude the company, size-banded within the industry. A MIC:TICKER of a company no US exchange lists is priced on its own cap and reports: P/E, Price/Sales and Price/Book, each on TTM or its newest fiscal year as labelled, without EV or peers. Use GetValuationMultiplesHistory for history.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:MC) for a listing outside the US.

tools.name: GetValuationMultiplesHistory
tools.title: Valuation Multiples History
tools.description: Get up to ~10 years of quarterly EV/Revenue, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA, P/E, Price/Sales and Price/Book, with P/FFO and P/AFFO for REITs and EV/Adjusted EBITDA for verified filers. Each row is recomputed at its filing date from facts then available and that day's raw close; non-GAAP cells name their TTM or fiscal-year basis. Completed exact-primary split reconciliation preserves older samples; anchors before an unresolved split are omitted. The reply reports omissions and missing EV inputs by cause. Uses the strict USD-only TTM/EV methodology of GetValuationMultiples on one effective split basis. A MIC:TICKER of a company no US exchange lists gets P/E only: its own close over the EPS filed by each date. Missing or unproved inputs are dashes, never estimates.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XTKS:9983) for a listing outside the US.

tools.name: GetVixHistory
tools.title: VIX Volatility Index History
tools.description: Get CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) historical daily OHLC data. VIX measures expected 30-day S&P 500 volatility. Below 15 = low volatility/complacency, above 30 = high fear/uncertainty. Data available from 1990 to present.

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to 3 months ago)

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to latest available)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of records to return (default: 60, max: 500). When the range holds more rows the newest are kept; rows are always listed oldest to newest.

tools.name: GetWebDataFeed
tools.title: Get Tracker
tools.description: Get the latest independently verified stored result for one of the caller's trackers, or the latest retained result at or before a requested timestamp. This is read-only, never triggers a live run, and preserves the last good result after a newer failure. To create or manage a tracker, tell the user to open the Equibles Portal and choose Dashboard → Trackers: https://www.equibles.com/trackers

dataFeed.description: The tracker name or full id shown by ListWebDataFeeds.

capturedAtOrBefore.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp. Returns the newest retained verified capture completed at or before this instant. Omit it for the latest result.

tools.name: ListCryptoAssets
tools.title: Crypto Coins
tools.description: List the crypto coins with prices, in symbol order: symbol, pair, whether it still trades and its first stored trade date. Coins are known by symbol only (BTC, ETH); there are no coin names, market caps or supplies. query keeps the symbols that start with it. Prices are in US dollars from one exchange. Use GetCryptoQuote for the latest price, GetCryptoPrices for daily candles and GetCryptoIntradayPrices for candles within the day. Included on every plan.

query.description: Start of a coin symbol, e.g. BT (default: every coin)

maxResults.description: Maximum coins to return (default: 100, max: 500)

offset.description: Coins to skip, for the next page (default: 0)

tools.name: ListExchanges
tools.title: Covered Exchanges
tools.description: List the markets listings are covered on: the US directory and each exchange outside the US, with the exchange codes its listings are written under (MIC:TICKER), its country code, trading currency, session hours and listing count. Use a code as SearchListings exchange or market.

tools.name: ListFilings
tools.title: List Filings
tools.description: List stored SEC filings and earnings-call transcripts newest first. Omit ticker for a market-wide feed or provide one ticker for a company-specific list. Returns company identity, document IDs, types, filing and reporting dates, SEC item numbers, line counts, EDGAR accession numbers and acceptance times (UTC; blank for filings stored before October 2026), and page totals. Supports date, document-type, and exact SEC item-number filters. Hidden document types remain excluded unless explicitly requested. When the deployment summarizes documents, each row adds a short summary of what the document says, and when it has a public document viewer, each row adds the filing's page URL to share with the user. Pass a returned ID to SearchDocument or ReadDocumentLines.

ticker.description: Optional company ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT); a listing outside the US is MIC:TICKER (e.g. XPAR:AIR), whose list includes its ESEF reports. Omit for all companies.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of documents per page (default: 10)

startDate.description: Optional start date filter in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: Optional end date filter in YYYY-MM-DD format

documentType.description: Document type filter: a registered value such as 'TenK', 'TenQa', 'EightK', 'TwentyF', 'Def14A', 'Defa14A', 'SThree' or 'TenderOfferThirdParty', or its SEC form name ('10-K', '20-F/A', 'DEFA14A', 'S-3ASR', 'SC TO-T', 'NT 10-Q'), plus deployment-registered types such as EarningsCallTranscript. An unrecognized value returns an error listing every accepted value.

itemNumber.description: Optional exact SEC current-report item number, e.g. 2.02, 5.02, or 1.01.

tools.name: ListForexPairs
tools.title: Forex Pairs
tools.description: List the forex currency pairs with rates, in pair order: pair (EUR/USD), both currencies' names, whether it still trades and its first stored trade date. A rate is the price of one unit of the first currency in the second, from one exchange's trades, not an interbank or official reference rate. currency keeps the pairs that include it. Use GetForexQuote for the latest rate, GetForexPrices for daily candles and GetForexIntradayPrices for candles within the day. Included on every plan.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR, to keep the pairs that include it (default: every pair)

maxResults.description: Maximum pairs to return (default: 100, max: 500)

offset.description: Pairs to skip, for the next page (default: 0)

tools.name: ListInvestorEvents
tools.title: Browse Investor Events
tools.description: List a company's investor events, newest first: earnings calls plus conferences, investor days and shareholder meetings. Each row gives the event id, type, UTC start, title, fiscal period (earnings calls only), status, and each material's status (available, pending, notPublished, failed, notAttempted, noCallHeld) for transcript, audio and slides. Read a conference by event id with GetInvestorEventTranscript; GetEarningsCallEvent is keyed by fiscal quarter.

ticker.description: Company ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:AIR) for a listing outside the US.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 25, max 100; values outside 1-100 are clamped)

eventType.description: Optional event type to filter on: EarningsCall, CapitalMarketsDay, InvestorUpdate, AGM, Conference, FiresideChat, or MAndA (default: all types)

offset.description: Number of matching events to skip before returning rows (default 0)

includeUncaptured.description: Also list events hidden because none of their materials could be captured and still on the company's own IR calendar (default false); their status reads Unavailable.

tools.name: ListWebDataFeeds
tools.title: List Trackers
tools.description: List the caller's own trackers (recurring, verified website data collections), with schedule, state, visibility, and most recent run. This is read-only and never contacts a source website. To create or manage one, tell the user to open the Equibles Portal and choose Dashboard → Trackers: https://www.equibles.com/trackers

tools.name: LoadReaderPart
tools.title: Load Reader Part
tools.description: Used by the Equibles filing reader already on screen to load the part its reader scrolls to. Not for answering a question: ShowFiling opens a filing and ReadDocumentLines returns its text.

split.description: The cut of it the reader holds.

tools.name: ReadDocumentLines
tools.title: Read Filing Lines
tools.description: Read numbered lines from one SEC filing or earnings-call transcript. Use line numbers returned by SearchDocument or request a known range. Returns at most 2,000 lines and identifies the next startLine when truncated.

endLine.description: Last line to read (1-based, inclusive). At most 2,000 lines are returned per call; a longer range is truncated with a note on how to continue.

tools.name: RefreshCard
tools.title: Refresh Equibles Card
tools.description: Used by the buttons on an Equibles card already on screen to load another range or view into that card. Not for answering a question: to show the user a card, call one of the Show tools.

tool.description: The data tool the card is drawn from.

arguments.description: That tool's arguments, as one object.

tools.name: RemovePortfolioLot
tools.title: Remove Portfolio Lot
tools.description: Permanently delete a lot from the USER's portfolio, as if it had never been recorded. This is for a lot entered by mistake. It is NOT how a sale is recorded: deleting a lot that was sold destroys its realized profit; use ClosePortfolioLot for that. This cannot be undone, so confirm with the user first, naming the lot.

portfolio.description: The portfolio holding the lot, by name.

lotId.description: The lot id shown by GetMyPortfolio, e.g. a1b2c3d4.

tools.name: ReportProblem
tools.title: Report an Equibles Tool Problem
tools.description: Report an Equibles tool call you actually made when it failed, timed out, was unexpectedly empty (ToolFailed), or returned verifiably impossible or contradictory data (ImplausibleResult). Answer the user first, then retry or use a fallback; this report does not fix the current call. Report the call and response, never the person or their question. Omit private or user-provided argument values or replace them with [redacted]. Mention briefly that you flagged it. Do not report surprising-but-plausible data, missing tools, feature requests, or non-Equibles tools.

problemKind.description: Either 'ToolFailed' (error, timeout, or unexpectedly empty) or 'ImplausibleResult' (answered, but the data cannot be right).

toolName.description: The Equibles tool that misbehaved, e.g. GetCompanyKpis.

observation.description: What went wrong, in one or two sentences: the error text, or why the figures are not credible. Describe the call and its response only — never the user or their question. Do not submit placeholder-only text such as N/A.

expected.description: Optional. What you expected instead, and how you know — a figure from another Equibles tool, a filing, or the tool's own documented behaviour. This is what makes an implausible-result report reproducible.

arguments.description: Optional. The arguments you passed to the failing tool, as JSON or key=value pairs, so the call can be replayed. Omit or redact any user-provided or private text.

tools.name: ScreenStocks
tools.title: Stock Screener
tools.description: Screen listed stocks with optional min/max bounds for price, market cap, institutional ownership, 13F holder signals (conviction, crowding, private-fund adviser ownership, active holders' share change, holder tenure and price versus the holders' estimated cost), short data, insider activity, valuation, growth, margins, liquidity and earnings. Exact sector, industry, covered-index membership and going-concern filters are also available. A stock missing a bounded metric is excluded. Results use the requested sort (market cap descending by default), are paged, and include each dataset's vintage. Filtering or sorting on a fundamental metric adds that metric to the result table. For what the bounds cannot express (moving averages, price change, returns, leverage, one metric against another) pass formula; the bounds are never limited by plan. US listings by default; pass market to screen European, Chinese, Hong Kong, Japanese or Canadian listings.

minFilerCount.description: Minimum number of 13F institutional filers holding the stock.

maxFilerCount.description: Maximum number of 13F institutional filers holding the stock.

minFilerDelta.description: Minimum quarter-over-quarter change in filer count.

maxFilerDelta.description: Maximum quarter-over-quarter change in filer count.

minShortInterestPercent.description: Minimum short interest as a percent of shares outstanding (0-100).

maxShortInterestPercent.description: Maximum short interest as a percent of shares outstanding (0-100).

minSqueezeScore.description: Minimum composite short-squeeze score (0-100, peer-relative; higher = more squeeze-prone).

minInsiderSentiment.description: Minimum composite insider-sentiment score (0-100, peer-relative; higher = more aggressive insider accumulation).

minNetInsiderBuy.description: Minimum net open-market insider buying by officers and directors in dollars over the trailing 90 days.

maxNetInsiderBuy.description: Maximum net open-market insider buying by officers and directors in dollars over the trailing 90 days.

hasGoingConcernDoubt.description: True keeps only companies whose latest filing states unalleviated going-concern doubt; false keeps only companies without the flag.

sector.description: Exact sector name (e.g. Technology, Healthcare). An unknown name returns the accepted list.

industry.description: Exact industry name (e.g. Semiconductors). Prefer sector for broad groups.

index.description: Keep only members of one covered index, by slug or name (sp-500, S&P 500, nasdaq-100, Russell 2000). An unknown name returns the accepted list.

maxPe.description: Maximum trailing-twelve-month price-to-earnings ratio (e.g. 15 for value screens).

minDividendYield.description: Minimum trailing dividend yield in percent (e.g. 3 = 3%).

maxDividendYield.description: Maximum trailing dividend yield in percent.

minRevenueGrowth.description: Minimum revenue growth in percent, latest quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier.

maxRevenueGrowth.description: Maximum revenue growth in percent, latest quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier.

minDollarVolume.description: Minimum trailing-3-month average daily dollar volume in dollars (e.g. 5000000 = $5M/day).

maxDollarVolume.description: Maximum trailing-3-month average daily dollar volume in dollars.

minNetIncome.description: Minimum trailing-twelve-month net income in dollars (0 keeps profitable companies only).

maxNetIncome.description: Maximum trailing-twelve-month net income in dollars.

minInstitutionalOwnership.description: Minimum institutional ownership: 13F shares held over shares outstanding, in percent (overlapping filings can exceed 100).

minConvictionShare.description: Minimum conviction share: percent of the stock's 13F filers holding it among their ten largest positions.

minCrowding.description: Minimum crowding: shares held by high-turnover 13F filers and private-fund advisers, in percent of shares outstanding.

maxCrowding.description: Maximum crowding in percent of shares outstanding.

minPrivateFundOwnership.description: Minimum ownership by 13F filers that advise private funds (Form ADV), in percent of shares outstanding.

maxPrivateFundOwnership.description: Maximum private-fund adviser ownership in percent of shares outstanding.

minActiveHolderChange.description: Minimum like-for-like share change of actively managed 13F holders over the quarter, in percent (positive = adding).

maxActiveHolderChange.description: Maximum like-for-like share change of actively managed 13F holders, in percent.

minHolderTenure.description: Minimum value-weighted holder tenure in quarters (how long 13F filers have held the stock).

maxHolderTenure.description: Maximum value-weighted holder tenure in quarters.

minEstimatedCostGap.description: Minimum quarter-end price versus the 13F holders' ESTIMATED average cost, in percent (negative = holders sit on an estimated loss).

maxEstimatedCostGap.description: Maximum quarter-end price versus the holders' estimated average cost, in percent.

sortBy.description: Sort key: marketcap, ticker, name, price, filers, filerdelta, sipct, dtc, squeeze, sentiment, insiderbuy, pe, divyield, revgrowth, grossmargin, dollarvol, netincome, instown, conv, crowd, pfown, actlfl, tenure or costgap, or any formula metric key (change30d, roic, fcfyield). Default marketcap. An unknown key is rejected with the accepted keys, never silently ignored.

maxResults.description: Maximum rows to return (default 50; clamped to 1-200).

page.description: Result page (default 1) — combine with maxResults to walk past the first page of a large match set.

tickers.description: Optional list of up to 200 tickers to restrict the screen to (stocks the user holds or follows); every other bound and sortBy still apply. Class-share dots (BRK.B) resolve to the listed form and a secondary listing to its issuer; an uncovered symbol, or a covered one the screen leaves out, is named back with the reason. A non-US listing is MIC:TICKER (XTSE:SHOP, XPAR:AIR) or its exchange-suffixed symbol (0700.HK, SAP.DE); naming one screens every market unless market is set.

market.description: Listing markets as ISO country codes, comma-separated (e.g. GB,FR or CN,HK), or 'all'. Default US. A non-US row's ticker is a qualified MIC:TICKER symbol (e.g. XPAR:AIR) that the portfolio, price, financial, earnings-call, guidance, debt and estimate tools accept; its price and market cap are USD at the official rate, with the local close beside the price. Non-US rows carry price data only, except a company also listed in the US, whose home listing adds its company figures.

formula.description: One boolean rule over screener metric keys, applied with the other arguments: comparisons, + - * /, parentheses, AND, OR, NOT, e.g. pricesma50 > 0 AND change30d > 10 AND roic > 15. Percents are plain numbers (20 = 20%); pricesma50 and pricesma200 are the price's percent distance from its 50- and 200-day average. A stock missing a metric never matches; an unknown key is answered with every key. Without Pro: up to 3 plain conditions joined by one AND or OR. Named metrics join the table.

columns.description: Extra result columns as formula metric keys, comma-separated (e.g. roic,fcfyield,change1y), up to 12. An unknown key is answered with every key.

tools.name: SearchBrazilianFunds
tools.title: Search Brazilian Funds
tools.description: Find Brazilian investment funds by words of their name, accents optional (e.g. 'previ acoes', 'verde'), or by their 14-digit register number, largest net assets first: each fund's name, manager, asset class, newest reported month, net assets in reais and slug. Pass the slug to GetBrazilianFundPortfolio for the fund's share portfolio. For US registered funds use SearchFunds; for the Brazilian funds holding one B3 share use GetBrazilianFundHoldings.

query.description: Words of the fund's name (all must appear, accents optional), or its register number with or without punctuation.

maxResults.description: Maximum funds, largest net assets first (default 20, max 50).

offset.description: Rows to skip for paging (default 0).

tools.name: SearchCftcMarkets
tools.title: Search CFTC Futures Contracts
tools.description: Search the tracked CFTC futures contracts by name, market code, common contract name, or standard futures symbol, or omit the query to list every tracked contract. Coverage is a curated set of ~35 major contracts across Agriculture, Energy, Metals, Equity Indices, Interest Rates, and Currencies - markets outside this set have no COT data here. Returns matching contracts with their codes and categories; use this to discover market codes before calling GetCftcPositioning.

query.description: Search query — market code, name words, common name, or standard symbol (e.g., 'gold futures', 'WTI', 'ES', 'S&P 500', '088691'). Search requires every punctuation-independent word first and broadens to any word only when no strict row matches. Omit to list all tracked contracts.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50, max: 500)

tools.name: SearchCongressMembers
tools.title: Search Congress Members
tools.description: Search the tracked congressional roster by name. Search first requires every punctuation-independent query word anywhere in the filed name, then broadens to any word only when no strict row matches. Verified public-name aliases such as Dan Crenshaw resolve to the roster name. Returns each match with its position, seat and current party (from the latest term); pass the returned exact Name to GetMemberTrades or GetMemberNetWorth.

query.description: Search query — partial or full name (e.g., 'Pelosi', 'Cruz', 'Dan')

position.description: Filter by position: Senator or Representative (defaults to both)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 20, max: 500)

tools.name: SearchDocument
tools.title: Search Within One Filing
tools.description: Search one SEC filing or earnings-call transcript by document ID. semantic mode uses hybrid relevance and returns excerpts in document order with approximate line numbers. exact mode performs a literal case-insensitive substring match and returns precise matching lines. Get document IDs from SearchDocuments or ListFilings; use ReadDocumentLines for surrounding text.

query.description: Search query — plain keywords or a short natural-language phrase. When too few excerpts match every word, the search automatically broadens to match any of the words. In searchMode 'exact', matched as a literal case-insensitive substring.

documentId.description: Document ID obtained from ListFilings or a SearchDocuments result header

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

maxExcerptChars.description: Maximum characters per excerpt (default: 0 = full excerpt). Set a small value (e.g. 400) for a compact scan across many results; truncated excerpts end with an explicit note.

searchMode.description: How to match: 'semantic' (default — hybrid keyword and semantic relevance) or 'exact' (literal case-insensitive substring match with precise line numbers).

tools.name: SearchDocuments
tools.title: Search SEC Filings
tools.description: Search SEC filings and earnings-call transcripts with hybrid keyword and semantic retrieval, or with match 'phrase' for only the excerpts containing an exact phrase. Omit ticker to search every company, or provide one ticker to search only that company. Returns excerpts with document IDs for SearchDocument or ReadDocumentLines. Use excludeTickers and maxResultsPerCompany only for market-wide discovery; use ListFilings to browse filings newest first without a text query.

query.description: Search query — plain keywords or a short natural-language phrase. In ranked mode, when too few excerpts match every word, the search automatically broadens to match any of the words; concise, filing-phrased terms (e.g. 'Data Center revenue') still rank best. In phrase mode, the exact phrase to find.

ticker.description: Optional company ticker; a listing outside the US is MIC:TICKER (e.g. XPAR:AIR). Omit to search across all companies.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5, max: 500)

documentTypes.description: Optional document types. Accepts registered values such as TenK, TenQ, EightK, TwentyF, SixK, FortyF, Def14A, SOne, or deployment-registered types such as EarningsCallTranscript. SEC form names such as 10-K, DEFA14A, S-3, SC TO-T or NT 10-K are also accepted; an invalid value returns the full accepted list.

startDate.description: Optional start date filter in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: Optional end date filter in YYYY-MM-DD format

excludeTickers.description: Optional tickers to exclude from a market-wide search (max 25). Cannot be combined with ticker.

maxResultsPerCompany.description: Maximum results from any single company (default: 0 = unlimited). Set a small value (e.g. 2) to spread results across more companies for discovery-style queries.

maxExcerptChars.description: Maximum characters per excerpt (default: 0 = full excerpt). Set a small value (e.g. 400) for a compact scan across many results; truncated excerpts end with an explicit note.

match.description: How the query matches: 'ranked' (default — relevance-ranked keyword and semantic retrieval that broadens to any of the words when results are sparse) or 'phrase' (only excerpts containing the query's words consecutively and in order; case and punctuation are ignored).

tools.name: SearchEconomicIndicators
tools.title: Search Economic Indicators
tools.description: Search the curated set of US macro series from FRED and Canadian series from FRED, the Bank of Canada and Statistics Canada that Equibles tracks (rates, inflation, employment, GDP, housing, market indicators) — not the full FRED catalog. Search first requires every punctuation-independent query word anywhere across the series ID, title, or category, then broadens to any word only when that strict search has no rows. Standard names such as fed funds rate, jobless claims, payrolls, yield curve, and core CPI are recognized; the tracked interest rates include the effective federal funds rate (EFFR), the Federal Reserve's FOMC target range upper and lower bounds, SOFR and IORB. An empty query lists every tracked series. Results include seasonal adjustment, the latest observation date, and the UTC time Equibles last synced the series.

query.description: Search query — series ID, title keyword, or category name (e.g., 'inflation', 'unemployment', 'GDP', 'FEDFUNDS'). Empty lists all tracked series.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 20, max: 500)

tools.name: SearchEtfs
tools.title: Search ETFs
tools.description: Search active exchange-traded funds and products by ticker, fund name, sponsor, or ISIN, US and other exchanges. US ETF identity comes from the authoritative security-type reference directory, with assets and holdings from the linked SEC Form NPORT-P fund series when available; a fund listed on another exchange is named MIC:TICKER (for example XETR:SXR8) with its currency and ISIN. US matches come first. Use GetEtfProfile for analysis, GetStockPrices for a fund's price history, or GetEtfHoldings for the portfolio.

query.description: Ticker, fund name, sponsor, or ISIN (for example SPY, S&P 500, iShares, SXR8, or IE00B5BMR087).

exchange.description: Market identifier code of one exchange outside the US to search alone (for example XETR); omit to search the US first, then other exchanges.

maxResults.description: Maximum results to return (default 20, max 500).

tools.name: SearchFunds
tools.title: Search Funds and ETFs
tools.description: Search the tracked SEC Form NPORT-P fund directory by fund name, ticker, SEC series ID, or registrant. Returns one canonical profile per series with ticker, registration type, latest report date, assets, and reported-versus-stored holding counts. Exact stored tickers outrank verified share-class aliases. Use the profile ID with GetFundProfile. The directory covers NPORT-P filers; a miss is a dataset-coverage result, not proof that a fund does not exist.

query.description: Fund name, ticker, registrant, or verified share-class alias (e.g., 'Russell 2000', 'iShares', 'IWM', 'VOO').

maxResults.description: Maximum number of funds to return, largest by net assets first (default: 20, max: 500)

tools.name: SearchInsiders
tools.title: Search Corporate Insiders
tools.description: Search the tracked SEC corporate-insider set (directors, officers, 10% owners) by name. Search first requires every punctuation-independent whole query word in the filed legal name, then broadens to any whole word only when no strict row matches; a token inside a different word is not a match. Verified public-name aliases such as Jensen Huang resolve to the SEC owner identity. Returns CIK, role, latest filing company, and location, ordered by recent filing activity.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results (default: 10, max: 500; values outside 1-500 are clamped)

offset.description: Number of matches to skip before returning rows (default: 0, clamped to 0-100000). For the next page, add the returned row count to the clamped current offset; if the next offset exceeds 100000, narrow the filters instead. Stop when fewer than the effective page size (maxResults clamped to 1-500) are returned, or the response's total has been reached.

tools.name: SearchInstitutions
tools.title: Search Institutional Investors
tools.description: Search the tracked 13F filer set by institution name or SEC CIK. Search first requires every punctuation-independent query word anywhere in the filed name, then broadens to any word only when no strict row matches. Verified brand aliases such as Fidelity, Vanguard, and BlackRock include their current flagship CIK. Results are largest within the recently-active filing bucket first and include latest report date, tracked 13F position value, and position count so same-name filers can be compared before calling an institution tool. Values use report-date closing prices, may fall back to filer values, and can be zero when unvalued. Scoped institution tools remain strict and never discard an unmatched word. Each result shows its entity type from regulatory records, and holderTypes filters by it.

query.description: Search query — institution name, partial name, or CIK

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, clamped to 1-500)

holderTypes.description: Holder types to keep, as an array of tokens: adv (registered investment adviser), era (exempt reporting adviser), ia (other adviser), bank, ins (insurer), bd (broker-dealer), fund (registered fund), plan (benefit plan), nonus (non-US institution), hc (parent holding company or control person with no other type on record), unk (no deciding record yet), e.g. ["bank", "ins"]. Types come from Form ADV, SEC filer profiles, 13D/13G and N-CEN, never from names. Omit for all.

tools.name: SearchInvestmentAdvisers
tools.title: Search Investment Advisers
tools.description: Search the tracked SEC Form ADV adviser set by firm name. Search first requires every punctuation-independent query word anywhere in the legal or business name, then broadens to any word only when no strict row matches. Returns CRD, main office, regulatory assets under management, employee count and as-of date, largest by assets first. Use the CRD with GetInvestmentAdviser.

query.description: Part of the firm's legal or business name (e.g., "Vanguard", "Renaissance")

maxResults.description: Maximum number of advisers to return (default: 20, clamped to 1-500)

tools.name: SearchListings
tools.title: Listing Search
tools.description: Find exchange listings by company name or ticker (query), by ISIN (isin), or list every listing of one exchange or country, across the US and other exchanges. Each row gives the symbol other tools accept (a bare ticker for a US listing, MIC:TICKER such as XETR:SIE for another exchange), the company, country, trading currency, ISIN, security type and whether it is the company's main listing. An ISIN returns every listing of that security, each in its own currency; a US or Canadian ISIN also matches a US listing by its CUSIP. Use ListExchanges for the exchange and country codes.

query.description: Company name or ticker to search for (e.g. siemens, ASML, XETR:SIE).

isin.description: ISIN to look up (e.g. IE00B5BMR087); not combined with query.

exchange.description: Exchange code to keep or list (e.g. XETR, XAMS, XLIS); see ListExchanges.

market.description: Country code whose listings to list (e.g. US, DE, PT); used on its own.

maxResults.description: Maximum rows to return (default 20, max 500).

offset.description: Rows to skip before returning results (default 0).

tools.name: ShowEarningsCall
tools.title: Show Earnings Call
tools.description: Opens an earnings call in the chat for the user: the recording with its synced transcript. Call it when the user asks to open, play, hear or read along with a call. Never call it to read a call yourself: GetEarningsCallTranscript returns the text and GetEarningsCallEvent the call's details.

ticker.description: Company ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:AIR) for a listing outside the US.

fiscalYear.description: Company fiscal year. Omit both period fields for the latest call.

tools.name: ShowEconomicChart
tools.title: Show Economic Chart
tools.description: Draws one economic series over time in the chat as an interactive chart, e.g. unemployment, CPI or the federal funds rate, as published or as its change from a year earlier (inflation from CPI). Call it when the user asks to see or plot an indicator, or when that chart is itself the answer. Find the series id with SearchEconomicIndicators. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetEconomicIndicator returns the observations.

seriesId.description: FRED series id, e.g. UNRATE, CPIAUCSL, FEDFUNDS.

startDate.description: First observation date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: the data tool's default range).

endDate.description: Last observation date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: latest).

transform.description: level (default): the values as published. yoy: the change from a year earlier, in percent, or in percentage points for a series stated in percent; use it for inflation from a price index such as CPIAUCSL.

tools.name: ShowFiling
tools.title: Show Filing
tools.description: Opens a filing in the chat for the user: a card with what it reports, and the filing as filed to read and search, with a quoted passage marked. Call it when the user asks to open, show, see or read a filing ("show me Nvidia's latest 8-K") or where a quote stands in it. When they ask for one part of it (a statement such as the balance sheet, or an item such as Risk Factors), pass section and it opens there. Get the documentId first from ListFilings, SearchDocuments or SearchDocument. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to read a filing yourself: ReadDocumentLines and SearchDocument return the text.

documentId.description: Document id from ListFilings or SearchDocuments.

fromLine.description: First line of the passage to open at, as numbered by ReadDocumentLines and SearchDocument. Omit to open at the top.

toLine.description: Last line of that passage (default: fromLine).

citedText.description: The passage's own words, copied from the filing, when you quote it in the answer.

section.description: A part of the filing to open at instead of a passage: an item ("Item 7", "Risk Factors") or a heading as the filing words it ("Consolidated Balance Sheets").

tools.name: ShowFinancialMetric
tools.title: Show Financial Metric
tools.description: Draws one reported financial metric in the chat as an interactive chart: its history for one company, or several companies side by side for one fiscal period or calendar year. Call it when the user asks to see or plot a metric such as revenue, net income or EPS, or when that chart is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetFinancialFact and CompareFinancialFact return the figures.

tickers.description: One ticker for a history, or several (max 25) to compare them; a listing on another exchange is MIC:TICKER (XPAR:AIR).

fiscalYear.description: Comparing several companies: the year compared, e.g. 2025. Not used for one company.

fiscalPeriod.description: FY or Q1..Q4. One company: optional filter. Several companies: the period compared (default FY).

basis.description: Comparing several companies: 'fiscal' (default) takes each company's fiscal year ending in fiscalYear, so a January year end covers mostly the year before; 'calendar' takes each company's fiscal year holding most of its days in fiscalYear (FY only). Use 'calendar' for a calendar year such as '2025 revenue'.

tools.name: ShowFinancialStatement
tools.title: Show Financial Statement
tools.description: Draws a company's income statement, balance sheet or cash-flow statement in the chat as an interactive table the user can switch between. Call it when the user asks to see a statement, or when the statement is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetFinancialStatement returns the figures.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT); a listing on another exchange is MIC:TICKER (XPAR:AIR).

year.description: Fiscal year as the company names it, e.g. 2023. Defaults to the latest period with line items.

period.description: Fiscal period: FY or Q1..Q4. Defaults to the latest period with line items.

tools.name: ShowInstitutionPortfolio
tools.title: Show Institution Portfolio
tools.description: Draws an institution's 13F portfolio in the chat as an interactive map and table of its positions. Call it when the user asks what an institution or fund manager owns, or when the portfolio is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetInstitutionPortfolio returns the figures.

reportDate.description: Quarter-end 13F report date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: the latest available).

tools.name: ShowInstitutionalBuyersSellers
tools.title: Show Institutional Buyers and Sellers
tools.description: Draws the institutions that bought and sold the most shares of a stock or ETF in a quarter in the chat, from 13F filings: the largest changes as bars and both ranked lists, with a way into each holder's portfolio and to other quarters. Call it when the user asks who has been buying or selling a stock, or when that list is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetTopInstitutionalBuyersSellers returns the figures.

ticker.description: Listed security ticker (e.g., AAPL, VOO).

reportDate.description: Quarter-end 13F report date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: the latest available).

tools.name: ShowOptionChain
tools.title: Show Option Chain
tools.description: Draws an option chain in the chat as an interactive table of calls and puts for one expiration. Call it when the user asks to see a chain, or when the chain is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetOptionChain returns the contracts.

ticker.description: Underlying stock or ETF ticker, e.g. NVDA.

expiration.description: Expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: the nearest expiration).

minStrike.description: Only include strikes at or above this price.

maxStrike.description: Only include strikes at or below this price.

type.description: Contract type: call or put (default: both).

tools.name: ShowPriceChart
tools.title: Show Price Chart
tools.description: Draws an interactive price chart in the chat for the user: a stock, ETF, coin, currency pair or the VIX, daily to intraday, as a line or candles with volume and indicator toggles. Call it when the user asks to see, plot or chart a price, or when a price chart is itself the answer ("how has NVDA done this year"). One symbol per chart. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetStockPrices, GetIntradayStockPrices, GetCryptoPrices and GetForexPrices return the figures.

symbol.description: What to chart: a stock or ETF ticker (AAPL, BRK-B, or MIC:TICKER such as XPAR:AIR), VIX, a coin (BTC) or a currency pair (EUR/USD).

market.description: stock (default; also ETFs and VIX), crypto or forex.

interval.description: Bar size: daily (default), weekly or monthly (stocks only), or an intraday size from 1min to 240min, e.g. 5min.

startDate.description: First day in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to one year back for daily stock bars and to the data tool's default otherwise.

endDate.description: Last day in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: latest).

style.description: How the chart opens: line (default) or candles. The user can switch on the card.

tools.name: ShowScreenerResults
tools.title: Show Screener Results
tools.description: Draws a stock screen's results in the chat as an interactive, sortable table. Call it when the user asks to see a screen or a list of stocks matching criteria, or when that table is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. ScreenStocks returns the rows.

filters.description: The screen, as one object holding exactly the arguments ScreenStocks takes, e.g. {"index":"sp-500","maxPe":15}.

tools.name: ShowSlideDeck
tools.title: Show Slide Deck
tools.description: Opens the slides of an earnings call or other investor event in the chat for the user. Call it when the user asks to open, show or see a presentation, deck or slides ("show me Nvidia's latest earnings slides"). Pass a ticker, with a fiscal period for a past call, or the event id of any investor event. Never call it to read slides yourself: GetInvestorEventSlideMetadata gives a deck's details, and SearchDocuments finds its text.

ticker.description: Company ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, MSFT), or MIC:TICKER (e.g., XPAR:AIR) for a listing outside the US. Omit when eventId is given.

fiscalYear.description: Company fiscal year. Omit both period fields for the latest earnings call with slides.

eventId.description: Investor event id, from ListInvestorEvents or GetEarningsCallEvent, for a conference or investor day.

tools.name: ShowTopHolders
tools.title: Show Top Holders
tools.description: Draws the largest institutional holders of a stock or ETF in the chat as an interactive table from 13F filings, with each holder's change and a way into its portfolio. Call it when the user asks who holds a stock, or when that list is itself the answer. Show at most one card per answer. Never call it to collect data for your own analysis: where the chat app draws cards it answers with one line, not the rows. GetTopHolders returns the figures.

ticker.description: Listed security ticker (e.g., AAPL, VOO).

reportDate.description: Quarter-end 13F report date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: the latest available).

tools.name: ShowUsageLimit
tools.title: Show Usage Limit
tools.description: Shows the user their Equibles account notice in the chat: daily requests used, when the allowance resets and the plans with a higher limit. Call it once when a tool answer says the daily limit was reached, or when the user asks about their Equibles usage or limit. It never counts against the limit.

tools.name: SuggestToolImprovement
tools.title: Suggest an Equibles Tool Improvement
tools.description: Suggest the smallest actionable contract improvement to an existing Equibles tool you actually called when it worked as documented but lacked a useful operation, filter, parameter or output option. Answer the user first; this records a future improvement and does not change the current call. Describe the call, never the person or their question. Omit private or user-provided argument values or replace them with [redacted]. Mention briefly that you suggested it. Use ReportProblem for wrong data; do not request new tools, duplicate existing options, or report non-Equibles ideas.

toolName.description: The existing Equibles tool you actually called, e.g. GetCompanyKpis.

limitation.description: The concrete limitation encountered in that call. State what the current operation, filter, parameter, or output contract could not do. Describe the call only — never the user or their question. Do not submit placeholder-only text such as N/A.

suggestedChange.description: The smallest actionable change you recommend, including the proposed operation, filter, parameter, or output behaviour and why it would resolve the limitation. Do not submit placeholder-only text such as N/A.

arguments.description: Optional. The arguments you passed to the existing tool, as JSON or key=value pairs, so the limitation can be reproduced. Omit or redact any user-provided or private text.

tools.name: UnwatchInstrument
tools.title: Unwatch Instrument
tools.description:
Remove a stock or an option contract from one of the USER's portfolio watchlists. This only removes the watch entry: it never touches a holding, so a stock the portfolio also owns stays exactly as recorded. Confirm with the user before removing.

Address the instrument the way it appears in GetMyPortfolio's Watching section: the symbol shown for a stock (MIC:TICKER for another exchange, e.g. XPAR:AIR), or the OCC symbol in optionContract for an option.

portfolio.description: The portfolio whose watchlist to remove from, by name.

ticker.description: The watched stock's symbol as shown, e.g. AAPL or XPAR:AIR. Omit when removing an option by its OCC symbol.

optionContract.description: Optional. The watched option's OCC symbol, e.g. O:AAPL260724C00110000. A U.S. and a Canadian contract can share one, so also pass ticker (the underlying as shown) when both are watched.

tools.name: UpdatePortfolioLot
tools.title: Update Portfolio Lot
tools.description:
Correct a lot the USER already recorded: a mistyped quantity, price, trade date, note or exchange rate. Only the fields you pass change; the rest are left alone.

The instrument itself cannot be edited: a lot on the wrong stock or the wrong contract is a different holding, so remove it with RemovePortfolioLot and add the right one. To record a sale, use ClosePortfolioLot rather than editing the quantity down, because editing it away loses the realized profit.

portfolio.description: The portfolio holding the lot, by name.

lotId.description: The lot id shown by GetMyPortfolio, e.g. a1b2c3d4.

quantity.description: Optional. The corrected signed size. Negative is a short or written option.

costPerUnit.description: Optional. The corrected price per share, always positive.

acquiredDate.description: Optional. The corrected trade date, as yyyy-MM-dd.

note.description: Optional. A replacement note, up to 256 characters.

fxRate.description: Optional. The broker's exchange rate on the trade, as units of the portfolio's currency per 1 unit of the lot's currency.

clearFxRate.description: Optional. True removes the broker's exchange rate, so the lot converts at the official rate on its trade date. Cannot be combined with fxRate.

tools.name: WatchInstrument
tools.title: Watch Instrument
tools.description:
Put a stock or an option contract on one of the USER's portfolio watchlists, without recording any position. A watched instrument shows up in GetMyPortfolio's 'Watching (not held)' section with a current mark and nothing else - no quantity, no cost, no value.

For a stock, pass its ticker, or MIC:TICKER for another exchange (e.g. XPAR:AIR). For an option, pass BOTH the underlying ticker and the OCC symbol in optionContract, exactly as AddPortfolioLot takes them; the contract is verified against the live options data before anything is stored.

Watching something the portfolio already holds is allowed - the page shows one row, and selling out later keeps the instrument on the list.

portfolio.description: The portfolio whose watchlist to add to, by name.

ticker.description: Stock ticker, or MIC:TICKER for a listing on another exchange, e.g. XPAR:AIR. For an option, the UNDERLYING's ticker, e.g. AAPL, or XTSE:RY for a Canadian contract.

optionContract.description: Optional. The OCC option symbol, e.g. O:AAPL260724C00110000. Provide it to watch an option contract; omit it for the stock itself.
